audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for mercy-giving, prayer, secrecy, Father language, Lord's Prayer, debts, fasting, treasures, eye/lamp imagery, Mammon, worry, birds/lilies, and seeking the reign and righteousness/justice.

verses.restored: Pay attention not to do your righteousness/justice before people in order to be seen by them; otherwise you have no reward with your Father in the heavens.

familiar.text: Take heed that ye do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise ye have no reward of your Father which is in heaven.

modern.text: “Be careful not to perform your righteous acts before men to be seen by them. If you do, you will have no reward from your Father in heaven.

original.text: Προσέχετε ⸀δὲ τὴν ⸀δικαιοσύνην ὑμῶν μὴ ποιεῖν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι αὐτοῖς· εἰ δὲ μή γε, μισθὸν οὐκ ἔχετε παρὰ τῷ πατρὶ ὑμῶν τῷ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.

verses.restored: Therefore when you give mercy-gifts, do not announce it dramatically as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and streets, so they may be honored by people. Amen, I say to you: they have received their reward.

familiar.text: Therefore when thou doest thine alms, do not sound a trumpet before thee, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may have glory of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.

modern.text: So when you give to the needy, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and on the streets, to be honored by men. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.

original.text: Ὅταν οὖν ποιῇς ἐλεημοσύνην, μὴ σαλπίσῃς ἔμπροσθέν σου, ὥσπερ οἱ ὑποκριταὶ ποιοῦσιν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς ῥύμαις, ὅπως δοξασθῶσιν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: But when you give mercy-gifts, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,

familiar.text: But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth:

modern.text: But when you give to the needy, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,

original.text: σοῦ δὲ ποιοῦντος ἐλεημοσύνην μὴ γνώτω ἡ ἀριστερά σου τί ποιεῖ ἡ δεξιά σου,

verses.restored: so that your mercy-gift may be in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will give back to you.

familiar.text: That thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward thee openly.

modern.text: so that your giving may be in secret. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you. The Lord’s Prayer (Luke 11:1–4)

original.text: ὅπως ᾖ σου ἡ ἐλεημοσύνη ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ ⸀κρυπτῷ ἀποδώσει ⸀σοι.

verses.restored: When you pray, you shall not be like the hypocrites, because they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and at the street corners so they may appear to people. Amen, I say to you: they have received their reward.

familiar.text: And when thou prayest, thou shalt not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.

modern.text: And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites. For they love to pray standing in the synagogues and on the street corners to be seen by men. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.

original.text: Καὶ ὅταν ⸂προσεύχησθε, οὐκ ἔσεσθε ὡς⸃ οἱ ὑποκριταί· ὅτι φιλοῦσιν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς γωνίαις τῶν πλατειῶν ἑστῶτες προσεύχεσθαι, ⸀ὅπως φανῶσιν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις· ἀμὴν λέγω ⸀ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσι τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: But you, when you pray, enter your inner room, shut your door, and pray to your Father in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will give back to you.

familiar.text: But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret; and thy Father which seeth in secret shall reward thee openly.

modern.text: But when you pray, go into your inner room, shut your door, and pray to your Father, who is unseen. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.

original.text: σὺ δὲ ὅταν προσεύχῃ, εἴσελθε εἰς τὸ ταμεῖόν σου καὶ κλείσας τὴν θύραν σου πρόσευξαι τῷ πατρί σου τῷ ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ ἀποδώσει ⸀σοι.

verses.restored: When praying, do not babble on like the nations, for they think they will be heard by their many words.

familiar.text: But when ye pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.

modern.text: And when you pray, do not babble on like pagans, for they think that by their many words they will be heard.

original.text: Προσευχόμενοι δὲ μὴ βατταλογήσητε ὥσπερ οἱ ἐθνικοί, δοκοῦσιν γὰρ ὅτι ἐν τῇ πολυλογίᾳ αὐτῶν εἰσακουσθήσονται·

verses.restored: Therefore do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask him.

familiar.text: Be not ye therefore like unto them: for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him.

modern.text: Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask Him.

original.text: μὴ οὖν ὁμοιωθῆτε αὐτοῖς, οἶδεν γὰρ ⸀ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὧν χρείαν ἔχετε πρὸ τοῦ ὑμᾶς αἰτῆσαι αὐτόν.

verses.restored: Therefore pray this way: Our Father in the heavens, let your name be made holy.

familiar.text: After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.

modern.text: So then, this is how you should pray: ‘Our Father in heaven, hallowed be Your name.

original.text: Οὕτως οὖν προσεύχεσθε ὑμεῖς· Πάτερ ἡμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς· ἁγιασθήτω τὸ ὄνομά σου,

verses.restored: Let your reign come; let your will come to be, as in heaven, also on earth.

familiar.text: Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.

modern.text: Your kingdom come, Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.

original.text: ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία σου, γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου, ὡς ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ⸀ἐπὶ γῆς·

verses.restored: Give us today our bread for the coming day / our needed bread.

familiar.text: Give us this day our daily bread.

modern.text: Give us this day our daily bread.

original.text: τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον δὸς ἡμῖν σήμερον·

verses.restored: And release us from our debts, as we also have released our debtors.

familiar.text: And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.

modern.text: And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.

original.text: καὶ ἄφες ἡμῖν τὰ ὀφειλήματα ἡμῶν, ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς ⸀ἀφήκαμεν τοῖς ὀφειλέταις ἡμῶν·

verses.restored: And do not bring us into testing, but rescue us from the harmful one.

familiar.text: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.

modern.text: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. ’

original.text: καὶ μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς πειρασμόν, ἀλλὰ ῥῦσαι ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ ⸀πονηροῦ.

verses.restored: For if you release people from their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also release you.

familiar.text: For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:

modern.text: For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.

original.text: ἐὰν γὰρ ἀφῆτε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τὰ παραπτώματα αὐτῶν, ἀφήσει καὶ ὑμῖν ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος·

verses.restored: But if you do not release people, neither will your Father release your trespasses.

familiar.text: But if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.

modern.text: But if you do not forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive yours. Proper Fasting

original.text: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἀφῆτε τοῖς ⸀ἀνθρώποις, οὐδὲ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ἀφήσει τὰ παραπτώματα ὑμῶν.

verses.restored: When you fast, do not become gloomy-faced like the hypocrites, for they alter their faces so they may appear to people as fasting. Amen, I say to you: they have received their reward.

familiar.text: Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.

modern.text: When you fast, do not be somber like the hypocrites, for they disfigure their faces to show men they are fasting. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.

original.text: Ὅταν δὲ νηστεύητε, μὴ γίνεσθε ⸀ὡς οἱ ὑποκριταὶ σκυθρωποί, ἀφανίζουσιν γὰρ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν ὅπως φανῶσιν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις νηστεύοντες· ἀμὴν λέγω ⸀ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: But you, when fasting, anoint your head and wash your face,

familiar.text: But thou, when thou fastest, anoint thine head, and wash thy face;

modern.text: But when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face,

original.text: σὺ δὲ νηστεύων ἄλειψαί σου τὴν κεφαλὴν καὶ τὸ πρόσωπόν σου νίψαι,

verses.restored: so that you may not appear to people as fasting, but to your Father in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will give back to you.

familiar.text: That thou appear not unto men to fast, but unto thy Father which is in secret: and thy Father, which seeth in secret, shall reward thee openly.

modern.text: so that your fasting will not be obvious to men, but only to your Father, who is unseen. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you. Treasures in Heaven (Luke 12:32–34)

original.text: ὅπως μὴ φανῇς τοῖς ἀνθρώποις νηστεύων ἀλλὰ τῷ πατρί σου τῷ ἐν τῷ ⸀κρυφαίῳ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ ⸁κρυφαίῳ ἀποδώσει σοι.

verses.restored: Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and decay consume and where thieves break in and take.

familiar.text: Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal:

modern.text: Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust destroy, and where thieves break in and steal.

original.text: Μὴ θησαυρίζετε ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ὅπου σὴς καὶ βρῶσις ἀφανίζει, καὶ ὅπου κλέπται διορύσσουσιν καὶ κλέπτουσιν·

verses.restored: But store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor decay consumes and where thieves do not break in or take.

familiar.text: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal:

modern.text: But store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where moth and rust do not destroy, and where thieves do not break in and steal.

original.text: θησαυρίζετε δὲ ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐν οὐρανῷ, ὅπου οὔτε σὴς οὔτε βρῶσις ἀφανίζει, καὶ ὅπου κλέπται οὐ διορύσσουσιν οὐδὲ κλέπτουσιν·

verses.restored: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

familiar.text: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

modern.text: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also. The Lamp of the Body (Luke 11:33–36)

original.text: ὅπου γάρ ἐστιν ὁ θησαυρός ⸀σου, ἐκεῖ ἔσται καὶ ἡ καρδία ⸁σου.

verses.restored: The lamp of the body is the eye. Therefore if your eye is single/clear/generous, your whole body will be full of light.

familiar.text: The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.

modern.text: The eye is the lamp of the body. If your eyes are good, your whole body will be full of light.

original.text: Ὁ λύχνος τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν ὁ ὀφθαλμός. ἐὰν οὖν ⸂ᾖ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ἁπλοῦς⸃, ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου φωτεινὸν ἔσται·

verses.restored: But if your eye is harmful, your whole body will be dark. Therefore if the light in you is darkness, how great is that darkness!

familiar.text: But if thine eye be evil, thy whole body shall be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great is that darkness!

modern.text: But if your eyes are bad, your whole body will be full of darkness. If then the light within you is darkness, how great is that darkness!

original.text: ἐὰν δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου πονηρὸς ᾖ, ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου σκοτεινὸν ἔσται. εἰ οὖν τὸ φῶς τὸ ἐν σοὶ σκότος ἐστίν, τὸ σκότος πόσον.

verses.restored: No one is able to serve two masters; for either he will reject the one and love the other, or hold to one and despise the other. You cannot serve the Divine and Mammon.

familiar.text: No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.

modern.text: No one can serve two masters: Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money. Do Not Worry (Luke 12:22–31)

original.text: Οὐδεὶς δύναται δυσὶ κυρίοις δουλεύειν· ἢ γὰρ τὸν ἕνα μισήσει καὶ τὸν ἕτερον ἀγαπήσει, ἢ ἑνὸς ἀνθέξεται καὶ τοῦ ἑτέρου καταφρονήσει. οὐ δύνασθε θεῷ δουλεύειν καὶ μαμωνᾷ.

verses.restored: Because of this I say to you: do not be worried for your life, what you will eat or drink, nor for your body, what you will wear. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothing?

familiar.text: Therefore I say unto you, Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on. Is not the life more than meat, and the body than raiment?

modern.text: Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat or drink; or about your body, what you will wear. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothes?

original.text: Διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν· μὴ μεριμνᾶτε τῇ ψυχῇ ὑμῶν τί ⸀φάγητε, μηδὲ τῷ σώματι ὑμῶν τί ἐνδύσησθε· οὐχὶ ἡ ψυχὴ πλεῖόν ἐστι τῆς τροφῆς καὶ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ ἐνδύματος;

verses.restored: Look at the birds of the heavens: they do not sow, reap, or gather into barns, and your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not worth more than they?

familiar.text: Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?

modern.text: Look at the birds of the air: They do not sow or reap or gather into barns—and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not much more valuable than they?

original.text: ἐμβλέψατε εἰς τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ὅτι οὐ σπείρουσιν οὐδὲ θερίζουσιν οὐδὲ συνάγουσιν εἰς ἀποθήκας, καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος τρέφει αὐτά· οὐχ ὑμεῖς μᾶλλον διαφέρετε αὐτῶν;

verses.restored: Which of you by worrying is able to add one cubit/span to his life?

familiar.text: Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit unto his stature?

modern.text: Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?

original.text: τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν μεριμνῶν δύναται προσθεῖναι ἐπὶ τὴν ἡλικίαν αὐτοῦ πῆχυν ἕνα;

verses.restored: And why are you worried about clothing? Learn from the lilies of the field, how they grow; they do not labor or spin.

familiar.text: And why take ye thought for raiment? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin:

modern.text: And why do you worry about clothes? Consider how the lilies of the field grow: They do not labor or spin.

original.text: καὶ περὶ ἐνδύματος τί μεριμνᾶτε; καταμάθετε τὰ κρίνα τοῦ ἀγροῦ πῶς ⸂αὐξάνουσιν· οὐ κοπιῶσιν οὐδὲ νήθουσιν⸃·

verses.restored: Yet I say to you that not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.

familiar.text: And yet I say unto you, That even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.

modern.text: Yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these.

original.text: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδὲ Σολομὼν ἐν πάσῃ τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ περιεβάλετο ὡς ἓν τούτων.

verses.restored: If the Divine clothes the grass of the field this way, alive today and tomorrow placed in the oven, will he not much more clothe you, ones of little trust?

familiar.text: Wherefore, if God so clothe the grass of the field, which to day is, and to morrow is cast into the oven, shall he not much more clothe you, O ye of little faith?

modern.text: If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, will He not much more clothe you, O you of little faith?

original.text: εἰ δὲ τὸν χόρτον τοῦ ἀγροῦ σήμερον ὄντα καὶ αὔριον εἰς κλίβανον βαλλόμενον ὁ θεὸς οὕτως ἀμφιέννυσιν, οὐ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς, ὀλιγόπιστοι;

verses.restored: Therefore do not be worried, saying, What shall we eat? or What shall we drink? or What shall we wear?

familiar.text: Therefore take no thought, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed?

modern.text: Therefore do not worry, saying, ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘What shall we wear?’

original.text: μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε λέγοντες· Τί φάγωμεν; ἤ· Τί πίωμεν; ἤ· Τί περιβαλώμεθα;

verses.restored: For the nations seek after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them all.

familiar.text: (For after all these things do the Gentiles seek:) for your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things.

modern.text: For the Gentiles strive after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them.

original.text: πάντα γὰρ ταῦτα τὰ ἔθνη ⸀ἐπιζητοῦσιν· οἶδεν γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος ὅτι χρῄζετε τούτων ἁπάντων.

verses.restored: But seek first the reign and righteousness/justice of the Divine, and all these things will be added to you.

familiar.text: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.

modern.text: But seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things will be added unto you.

original.text: ζητεῖτε δὲ πρῶτον τὴν ⸀βασιλείαν καὶ τὴν δικαιοσύνην αὐτοῦ, καὶ ταῦτα πάντα προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν.

verses.restored: Therefore do not be worried for tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Sufficient for the day is its own trouble.

familiar.text: Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.

modern.text: Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Today has enough trouble of its own.

original.text: μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε εἰς τὴν αὔριον, ἡ γὰρ αὔριον μεριμνήσει ⸀αὑτῆς· ἀρκετὸν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἡ κακία αὐτῆς.
